verdict: DENOISE TEST (denoise_test.py): would denoising the target (what within-line replicates buy) raise the ceiling? Scored against only the cross-line CONFIRMED-REAL part of each K562 response. 111 paired held-out KOs; 26% of a typical response is confirmed-real, the rest non-reproducing (noise or cell-specific). Restricting to the real subset: model recall 0.40->0.53 (+0.12), oracle 0.65->0.75 (+0.10). The model's MISSES are 79% non-reproducing and its HITS are 35% confirmed-real. So the ceiling is set largely by target NOISE: the model already finds the real movers and mostly misses the non-reproducing ones, so cleaner targets (WITHIN-line replicates) would raise the achievable recall and let the metric stop penalising unconfirmable calls. Replicates are the worthwhile data lever. (Raw counts are not in-repo, so a proper multi-guide re-aggregation would require fetching the raw Perturb-seq.) Deterministic.
